knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE)

A neighbour can act on a plant in two ways. In the variance-partition view
(the IGE model of `vignette("explicit-terms")`), each genotype carries an
indirect genetic effect, a random effect of its own, and nothing says what it
is made of. In the structural, trait-based view, the phenotype of a plant
responds to the *phenotypes* of its neighbours:

```
y = M y + X b + sum_k Z_k u_k + e,      M[(t,i),(u,j)] = Psi[t,u] * W_t[i,j]
```

`y` is in long format (one row per plant and trait). `Psi[t, u]` is the
effect of trait `u` of a neighbour (the **emitter**, a column of `Psi`) on
trait `t` of the focal plant (the **receiver**, a row), per unit of
neighbourhood weight `W_t[i, j]`. A diagonal entry is a loop: a tall
neighbour makes a plant taller, which makes its neighbours taller, and the
phenotypes are the equilibrium `y = (I - M)^-1 (X b + Z u + e)`.

With `A = I - M` invertible, `y* = A y` is an ordinary mixed model: mean
`X b`, covariance `V(theta)`. remlax therefore fits the structural model with
every term and residual structure it already has; only the objective changes,
and `Psi` becomes one more block of parameters.

## Three models

The examples below use one simulated field: 16 x 10 plants, queen
neighbourhood with unit weights (`s = 7.05` neighbours on average), 40
genotypes, two traits, `Psi[T1 <- T1] = 0.3 / s` (a loop) and
`Psi[T2 <- T1] = -0.6 / s`.

```{r}
library(remlax)
set.seed(2026)
nr <- 16; nc <- 10; N <- nr * nc; ng <- 40; q <- 2
field <- expand.grid(col = 1:nc, row = 1:nr)
W <- Matrix::Matrix((as.matrix(dist(field, method = "maximum")) == 1) * 1, sparse = TRUE)
s <- mean(Matrix::rowSums(W))
geno <- factor(sample(rep(sprintf("G%02d", 1:ng), length.out = N)))
Psi <- matrix(c(0.3, -0.6, 0, 0) / s, 2, dimnames = list(c("T1", "T2"), c("T1", "T2")))
a <- matrix(rnorm(ng * q), ng) %*% chol(matrix(c(1, 0.4, 0.4, 1), 2))
e <- matrix(rnorm(N * q), N)
eta <- as.numeric(a[as.integer(geno), ] + e) + rep(c(10, 20), each = N)
y <- as.numeric(solve(diag(N * q) - kronecker(Psi, as.matrix(W)), eta))
d <- data.frame(y = y, trait = factor(rep(c("T1", "T2"), each = N)),
                plant = rep(1:N, q), geno = rep(geno, q),
                row = factor(rep(field$row, q)), col = factor(rep(field$col, q)))
```

The incidences are built once. `place()` puts an `N x m` block on the rows of
one trait; that is how a multi-trait term gets one incidence per column of its
`Sigma`.

```{r}
X <- model.matrix(~ trait - 1, d)
Zg <- Matrix::sparseMatrix(i = 1:N, j = as.integer(geno), x = 1, dims = c(N, ng))
place <- function(Z, k) {
  zero <- Matrix::Matrix(0, N, ncol(Z), sparse = TRUE)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(1:q, function(j) if (j == k) Z else zero))
}
Z_DGE <- list(DGE_T1 = place(Zg, 1), DGE_T2 = place(Zg, 2))
Z_IGE <- list(IGE_T1 = place(W %*% Zg, 1), IGE_T2 = place(W %*% Zg, 2))
I_N <- Matrix::Diagonal(N) * 1
Z_plant <- list(res_T1 = place(I_N, 1), res_T2 = place(I_N, 2),
                IEE_T1 = place(W, 1), IEE_T2 = place(W, 2))
res_us <- rx_residual("us", trait = d$trait, unit = d$plant)
lag <- rx_lag(W, trait = d$trait, unit = d$plant)
```

### VP+: variance partition with a joint plant term

No lag. A genetic term over `[Z, W Z]` (direct and indirect genetic effects
and their covariance, `us` over `2q` columns) and a **plant term** over
`[I, W]`: its `2q x 2q` covariance holds the residual, the indirect
environmental effects (IEE) and their covariance. That term *is* the
residual, so the residual of the model is declared absent with
`rx_residual("none")`.

```{r}
vp <- rx_fit(rx_model(d$y, X, list(rx_term("gen", c(Z_DGE, Z_IGE), struct = "us"),
                                   rx_term("plant", Z_plant, struct = "us")),
                      residual = rx_residual("none")), backend = "cpu")
vp
```

```
Ajustement REML (cpu) : logLik -553.145225 | 20 parametres | 320 obs | 155.7 s
  max|grad| 8.48e-09 | decrement de Newton 1.40e-23 | 0 valeur(s) propre(s) negative(s)
  Sigma[gen] 4x4, diagonale : 3.7311 2.9334 0.4938 1.4171
  Sigma[plant] 4x4, diagonale : 0.813372 0.805986 0.018849 0.006307
  residuelle : aucune
  1 direction(s) plate(s) par construction (entrees de meme motif, seule leur somme est identifiee) : 19 parametres identifies
```

Without a residual, `V` must be positive definite from the terms alone. The
solver checks it at the starting values and stops with an explicit message
when it is not (for instance with a genetic term only).

With a symmetric `W`, `Cov(res_t, IEE_u)` and `Cov(res_u, IEE_t)` have the
same pattern in `V` and enter only through their sum: for `q >= 2` the plant
term has `q(q-1)/2` flat directions. The fit detects them from the incidences
(`fit$alias`), counts `q(q-1)/2` fewer parameters (`fit$n_par_identified`,
used by AIC, BIC and for the degrees of freedom of a likelihood ratio test),
keeps them out of the convergence verdict, and reports the identified sum:

```{r}
summary(vp)$varcomp[grepl("^plant", rownames(summary(vp)$varcomp)), ]
```

```
                         component   std.error     z.ratio bound
plant[1,1]             0.813372091 0.139307977  5.83866129     P
plant[2,1]             0.001297969 0.096644245  0.01343038     U
plant[2,2]             0.805986307 0.129325871  6.23221249     P
plant[3,1]             0.042702114 0.041785278  1.02194159     U
plant[3,2]            -0.097116894          NA          NA     N
plant[3,3]             0.018848987 0.015293000  1.23252389     P
plant[4,1]            -0.002427647          NA          NA     N
plant[4,2]            -0.071248677 0.042726551 -1.66755041     U
plant[4,3]             0.008366310 0.009706911  0.86189214     U
plant[4,4]             0.006306835          NA          NA     B
plant[3,2]+plant[4,1] -0.099544541 0.059816921 -1.66415355     U
```

`plant[3,2]` is `Cov(IEE_T1, res_T2)` and `plant[4,1]` is `Cov(IEE_T2, res_T1)`:
each is coded `N` (not identified on its own), their sum is estimated with a
standard error. The parametrisation is not constrained to a symmetric
residual-IEE block on purpose: a positive definite plant covariance with a
symmetric cross block is a strictly smaller model (a structural truth such as
`Cov(IEE, res) = Psi R_e` is not symmetric).

### TB: trait-based model

The lag carries the neighbour effects; the genetic term is the direct effect
only, and the residual is `us` over traits.

```{r}
tb <- rx_fit(rx_model(d$y, X, list(rx_term("gen", Z_DGE, struct = "us")), res_us, lag = lag),
             backend = "cpu")
tb
```

```
Ajustement REML (cpu) : logLik -494.836891 | 10 parametres | 320 obs | 24.9 s
  max|grad| 1.01e-04 | decrement de Newton 4.20e-11 | 0 valeur(s) propre(s) negative(s)
  Sigma[gen] 2x2, diagonale : 0.7416 0.5752
  residuelle : 0.9560 0.8858
  Psi (receveur en ligne, emetteur en colonne ; unites de W) | critere reml_y | log|det A| -0.910539 | rayon spectral de M 0.2930
          T1                   T2
    T1 <-    0.04670 (0.00540)    0.00539 (0.00909)
    T2 <-   -0.07835 (0.00529)   -0.01178 (0.00869)
```

The true values are `0.3 / 7.05 = 0.0426` and `-0.6 / 7.05 = -0.0851`; both
estimates are within 1.5 standard errors. Standard errors come from the
observed Hessian, as for the variance components, and the free entries of
`Psi` appear in the component table of `summary()`:

```{r}
summary(tb)$varcomp
```

```
                 component   std.error     z.ratio bound
gen[1,1]       0.741585235 0.224221704   3.3073749     P
gen[2,1]       0.199883061 0.147539928   1.3547727     U
gen[2,2]       0.575156162 0.183988331   3.1260469     P
residual[1,1]  0.956039130 0.124430002   7.6833490     P
residual[2,1]  0.050629466 0.084596151   0.5984843     U
residual[2,2]  0.885845251 0.114650526   7.7264822     P
Psi[T1<-T1]    0.046704934 0.005399027   8.6506210     U
Psi[T1<-T2]    0.005389221 0.009093886   0.5926203     U
Psi[T2<-T1]   -0.078349354 0.005291298 -14.8072084     U
Psi[T2<-T2]   -0.011776933 0.008692267  -1.3548747     U
```

Restricting `Psi` is done in `rx_lag()`: `struct = "diag"` (loops only),
`receivers =` and `emitters =` (subsets of traits), `struct = "mask"` with a
logical `q x q` matrix, and `value =` for entries held at a known value. The
free entries come last in `theta`, receiver by receiver, so `fixed_theta` can
also hold some of them at their starting value (`init =`).

### TB+: trait-based model with residual indirect genetic effects

Both routes: the lag, and a genetic term over `[Z, W Z]` whose indirect part
is the residual IGE, the part of a genotype's effect on its neighbours that
does not go through the measured traits.

```{r}
tbp <- rx_fit(rx_model(d$y, X, list(rx_term("gen", c(Z_DGE, Z_IGE), struct = "us")), res_us,
                       lag = lag), backend = "cpu")
tbp
```

```
Ajustement REML (cpu) : logLik -492.538658 | 17 parametres | 320 obs | 56.4 s
  max|grad| 1.06e-08 | decrement de Newton 2.93e-24 | 0 valeur(s) propre(s) negative(s)
  Sigma[gen] 4x4, diagonale : 0.757828 0.571184 0.015831 0.004371
  residuelle : 0.8510 0.8605
  Psi (receveur en ligne, emetteur en colonne ; unites de W) | critere reml_y | log|det A| -0.760373 | rayon spectral de M 0.2681
          T1                   T2
    T1 <-    0.04590 (0.00672)    0.00718 (0.01060)
    T2 <-   -0.07622 (0.00620)   -0.01524 (0.00978)
```

### TB+ with residual indirect environmental effects (IEE*)

A term over `W` placed on each trait adds the indirect environmental effects
not carried by the measured traits. The plant level is then VP+ in other
coordinates, and with both `Psi[t,u]` and `Psi[u,t]` free the direction of
transmission is only weakly identified; `rx_model()` warns:

```{r}
Z_iee <- list(IEE_T1 = place(W, 1), IEE_T2 = place(W, 2))
m <- rx_model(d$y, X, list(rx_term("gen", c(Z_DGE, Z_IGE), struct = "us"),
                           rx_term("iee", Z_iee, struct = "us")), res_us, lag = lag)
```

```
Warning message:
rx_model : terme(s) iee avec une incidence W (IEE*) et Psi libre dans les deux sens pour T1/T2. Le sens de la transmission n'y est que faiblement identifie (directions faibles de VP+) : laisser libre au plus une de Psi[t,u], Psi[u,t] (rx_lag(struct = "mask") ou receivers/emitters).
```

Leave at most one entry of each reciprocal pair free, here the hypothesised
path `T2 <- T1` and the loops:

```{r}
mk <- matrix(c(TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, TRUE), 2, dimnames = list(c("T1", "T2"), c("T1", "T2")))
lag_m <- rx_lag(W, trait = d$trait, unit = d$plant, struct = "mask", mask = mk)
tbi <- rx_fit(rx_model(d$y, X, list(rx_term("gen", c(Z_DGE, Z_IGE), struct = "us"),
                                    rx_term("iee", Z_iee, struct = "us")), res_us, lag = lag_m),
              backend = "cpu")
tbi
```

```
Ajustement REML (cpu) : logLik -492.625046 | 19 parametres | 320 obs | 163.3 s
  max|grad| 1.33e-08 | decrement de Newton 1.79e-22 | 0 valeur(s) propre(s) negative(s)
  Sigma[gen] 4x4, diagonale : 0.748706 0.569605 0.013158 0.004546
  Sigma[iee] 2x2, diagonale : 0.006178 0.002004
  residuelle : 0.818 0.846
  Psi (receveur en ligne, emetteur en colonne ; unites de W) | critere reml_y | log|det A| -1.686256 | rayon spectral de M 0.3787
          T1                   T2                  
    T1 <-    0.04945 (0.00389)    0.00000          
    T2 <-   -0.07648 (0.00625)   -0.01498 (0.00979)
```

Without IEE*, `Psi` is identified when full, through the genetic level, at
some cost in precision; a mask on the hypothesised paths still tightens it.

### TB with a spatially correlated environment

The lag goes through `rx_reml()` too, and combines with any residual the
formula grammar knows: here an unstructured covariance between traits times
a separable AR1 x AR1 field.

```{r}
tbs <- rx_reml(y ~ trait - 1, random = ~ us(geno), residual = ~ us(trait):ar1(row):ar1(col),
               data = d, trait = "trait", lag = lag, backend = "cpu")
tbs
```

```
Ajustement REML (cpu) : logLik -494.261208 | 12 parametres | 320 obs | 32.7 s
  max|grad| 4.14e-11 | decrement de Newton 7.38e-24 | 0 valeur(s) propre(s) negative(s)
  Sigma[geno] 2x2, diagonale : 0.7342 0.5622
  residuelle : 0.9576 0.8969
  Psi (receveur en ligne, emetteur en colonne ; unites de W) | critere reml_y | log|det A| -0.633419 | rayon spectral de M 0.2473
          T1                   T2
    T1 <-    0.04532 (0.00593)    0.00763 (0.00974)
    T2 <-   -0.07771 (0.00573)   -0.01322 (0.00924)
```

The rows of `rx_lag()` are those of `data`; `rx_reml()` refuses a lag when it
would have to drop incomplete rows, rather than realigning them silently.

## The criterion

The likelihood of `y` follows from that of `y*` by a change of variable, which
adds the Jacobian `log|det A|`. For maximum likelihood that is the whole story.
For REML it is not: the restricted likelihood of `y` is built on contrasts
orthogonal to the mean space of `y`, which is spanned by `X_y = A^-1 X`, not by
`X`. Harville's form of the restricted likelihood contains `|X'X|^{1/2}`,
constant in an ordinary model and usually dropped; here the factor is
`|X_y'X_y|^{1/2}`, and `X_y` depends on `Psi` as soon as the row sums of `W`
vary, which border plants always make them do. `rx_lag(criterion =)` offers:

| criterion | `-2 logL` | what it is |
|---|---|---|
| `"reml_y"` (default) | `-2 REML(y*) - 2 log|det A| - log|X_y'X_y| + log|X'X|` | the exact restricted likelihood of `y` |
| `"jacobian"` | `-2 REML(y*) - 2 log|det A|` | change of variable only, Harville's factor on `X` |
| `"ml"` | `-2 ML(y*) - 2 log|det A|` | maximum likelihood |

The extra term of `"reml_y"` is not a small-sample nuisance of order `1/N`: on
a field where the row sums of `W` vary, `X_y` is about `X / (1 - psi)` inside
the field, so the term is of order `log(1/(1 - psi))` per trait. Without it
the criterion depends on the scale of `b` in the `y*` parametrisation, and a
likelihood ratio between models with and without `Psi` carries that offset.
The fit reports the term (`fit$lag$logdet_mean`, in log-likelihood units)
whatever the criterion, together with `logLik_ystar` (REML of `y*` alone) and
`logLik_jacobian`. On the example:

```
reml_y   logLik  -494.8369  Psi[T1<-T1]  0.04670  Psi[T2<-T1] -0.07835  mean term 0.3071
jacobian logLik  -495.1378  Psi[T1<-T1]  0.04621  Psi[T2<-T1] -0.07821  mean term 0.2948
ml       logLik  -493.1208  Psi[T1<-T1]  0.04622  Psi[T2<-T1] -0.07824  mean term 0.2949
```

The estimates differ by a fraction of a standard error, as expected from
criteria that differ by a smooth function of `Psi`. Log-likelihoods are
comparable only within one criterion. Models without a lag (VP, VP+) have the
same value under `"reml_y"` and `"jacobian"`, which makes the default the one
to use for a likelihood ratio between VP+ and TB-type models.

## Trait means and border plants

With non-zero trait means, the structural model has mean
`E y = (I - M)^-1 X b`. Without feedback, the mean of trait `t` on plant `i`
is `mu_t + sum_u Psi[t,u] mu_u (W 1)_i`: plants with fewer neighbours (borders,
gaps) differ in mean. The three criteria above contain this term, because
they put the fixed effects in the structural equation. A model without a lag
(VP, VP+) does not, and its covariance ratio is then biased, by several
standard errors when the means are large relative to the standard deviations
(height is often 10 standard deviations away from zero). Conversely, with
large means a structural criterion reads much of `Psi` in the border pattern
of the mean, so that any border effect that is not an interaction (more light
at the edge) is attributed to `Psi`.

`rx_border(W, trait, unit)` returns the number of neighbours `W 1` (scaled by
its mean) as one fixed-effect column per trait. Add it to `X` of every model:

```r
X <- cbind(model.matrix(~ trait - 1, d), rx_border(W, d$trait, d$plant))
```

The VP-family models are then correct without feedback, and `Psi` of the
structural models is read from the covariances only, whatever the border
effects. With feedback, `order = 2` adds `W^2 1` and reduces the remaining
second-order terms. With constant row sums (torus, complete groups) the
columns are collinear with the intercepts and must not be added.

## How `log|det A|` is computed

Three exact paths, chosen once from the structure of the lag
(`fit$lag$path`):

* **no feedback** (`"nilpotent"`): the possible non-zero entries of `Psi` form
  a graph without a cycle (for instance only `T2 <- T1`). Then `M^q = 0`,
  `det A = 1` and `A^-1 = sum_{m<q} M^m`;
* **one symmetric W, complete data** (`"fast"`): `W = U diag(lambda) U'`
  once, and `log|det A| = sum_k log det(I_q - lambda_k Psi)`, `q x q` per
  eigenvalue;
* **otherwise** (`"general"`): one `W` per receiver trait (a list named by the
  traits), an asymmetric `W`, or missing (trait, plant) pairs: a dense LU of
  `A`, of the same order of cost as the Cholesky of `V` already paid at every
  evaluation.

The admissible region is the set of `Psi` reached from `Psi = 0` without
crossing a singular `A`: every real eigenvalue of `M` below 1. Outside it the
objective returns a large finite penalty, which the line search treats as a
cliff. On the eigenvalue path the condition is checked exactly at every
evaluation; on the general path only `det A > 0` is, and the exact condition is
checked at the end (`fit$lag$admissible`). The spectral radius of `M` is
reported; a value above 1 is allowed when all real eigenvalues are below 1
(the simultaneous model is defined, but the equilibrium is no longer the limit
of iterating `y <- M y + ...`). For one trait the region is the usual
parameter space of the SAR model, `psi` in `(1/lambda_min, 1/lambda_max)`;
for several traits it contains the stability region `rho(Psi) rho(W) < 1`.

## Checks and limits

The objective, under the three criteria and on the three paths, equals a
dense computation written independently in the tests; its gradient, through
`y* = A y` (the solver's analytic gradient with respect to `V` now also
returns `2 P y` for `y`), agrees with finite differences; a lag whose `Psi` is
held at zero reproduces the fit without lag bit for bit. VP+, TB and TB+ were
cross-validated against the independent engine of the IGE programme
(`igepath_reml`, eigenbasis and Woodbury), with and without feedback: same
log-likelihood under the same criterion and same estimates, to the
optimiser's tolerance.

Not available with a lag: Kenward-Roger, `rx_predict()` and `rx_scan()`, which
all assume `y` linear in `b` and `u` at given `V`. The mixed model equations
engine does not cover the lag either, and the dense engine fits it. `fitted()` and `residuals()` refer to `y*`
(`fit$ystar`). The Hessian is computed by finite differences of the gradient:
at an optimum close to the edge of the admissible region a step can cross it,
and the corresponding column of the Hessian is then wrong; the reported
spectral radius tells when that is a risk. A lagged model fitted with
`engine = "mme"` is fitted by the dense engine, with a message.
